title: INTEGRATED BUT DIVIDED: WHAT DID WE LOSE?

sense.text:
This is the scripture to meditate on through the whole class. “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation”: any kingdom where there is no unity is brought to destruction.

“And a house divided against a house falleth.” Inside your own house: you against your wife, your wife against you, your children against you and you against your children. That house is going to fall. It is going to be destroyed; it is not going to stand.

And that is what happened to our people. God is not a God of integration; God is a God of segregation, and segregation is all through the Bible, whatever the dumb pastors and the Christian church teach. Segregation is keeping different groups of people apart from one another: the signs went up, Black people cannot use this bathroom. Integration is combining separate parts into a single whole, and integration destroyed the black family and the black community. The worst thing that ever happened to black people in this country was integration. Put those signs back up.

During segregation we were forced to work with each other: I depend on you, you depend on me. Today the most difficult thing is getting black people to work together; they always find something to fight about. When you are asked who the enemy is, you point to the black man next to you, who never raped you, never killed you, never stole from you. During segregation we had the common sense to know who the enemy was. That is the division integration brought, and a house divided cannot stand. That is why the unity has to be brought back, and why Bishop Nathanyel always says we need to work together: the enemy does not want us to work together.

It is why black people still think the politicians can save us, voting Democrat or Republican. The politicians did not save us back then, and they are not going to save us today. A kingdom that is divided cannot stand.

Satan has a kingdom too. “If Satan also be divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand?” Satan cannot be divided against himself; if he were, his kingdom could not stand.

“Because ye say that I cast out devils through Beelzebub.” The Pharisees came against Christ and told him he cast out devils through the devil. That makes no sense: they were saying Satan’s own kingdom is divided against itself.
“And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your sons cast them out?” Christ insulted them. If you say I am casting out devils through Satan, what about your own children?

“Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty.” Black men are being found hanging from trees across this country, and in case after case they say the black man killed himself. Nobody knew that many black people could kill themselves like that. Lynching is back, and America says, I’m not guilty.

precepts.why:
“Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down.”

The accuser of our brethren is Esau, and he is cast down.

These lynchings and killings are not going to stop. Bishop has been teaching about this for years: first it was the police killings, now they are moving to lynching. It is the only way the Most High God is going to get our people to change. The so-called black leaders and the black church pretend it is not happening, hoping it will go away. And the white people doing the lynching are Christians, white nationalist Christians. You ain’t seen nothing yet. The Most High God is about to turn up the heat on our people: look at what is happening to the Haitians, and to the so-called Cubans in Miami who sang let’s vote for Donald Trump and are now being deported to Africa where they know nobody. That is not going to stop.

“As for us”: the us is the Israelites. “Our eyes as yet failed for our vain help.” We are seeking justice in an unjust system. We cry, we march, we scream, we boycott, and at the end of the day it is Merry Christmas and Happy Thanksgiving, and on Sunday you go back to the same slave master you are crying for justice against. That is mentally insane. We are like a pig with a bow tie: put a diamond chain on its neck, put the most expensive perfume on it, and it goes back to the dirt. No matter how much they murder us and rape us, we go back to them again.

“In our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us.” We are watching for a country that could not save us, waiting for an unjust system to give us justice. That is asking the rapist, the man who raped, stole and murdered, to go to court and convict himself. America built the perfect system, because it is their system, not ours. The system is against us.

Some pray for this to stop. We pray for it to continue. What they are trying to do is start a race war, and the government is not doing a damn thing about it. The president says nothing, the White House has issued no statement, and the media stays quiet. And it is not only down south; it is all over the country.

“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed.” The Most High has to reveal the white man, because some of our people’s heads are too deep in the white man’s rectum. Some still underestimate who this man is and have no idea how evil these people are. They are going to learn.

Why does God allow these lynchings to happen? Your opinion and your feelings don’t mean a damn thing; this is what the Bible says.

“See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me.” There is only one true God, the God of Israel, the God of the twelve tribes: the so-called Negroes, the so-called Hispanics, the so-called American Indians. That is our God.

“I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal.” Nobody has power to kill except God, because God is the only one who has the power to create. “Neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.” It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

So through all this chaos, our salvation is coming. We are not praying for peace, not for America, not for France, not for Europe, not for any of these countries. We are praying for vengeance for what they did to our people and are still doing right now, for God to destroy all our enemies. And if you are on our enemy’s side, you are our enemy too. Until our brothers and sisters repent, they are our enemies also, because many of our own people want to kill us for saying Jesus Christ is a black man, that salvation is only for the twelve tribes, brother get married and take care of your family, sister stop being a hoe and get a husband.

sense.text:
“Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me.” We take counsel, but not according to the Bible, not of the Most High.

“That they may add sin to sin.” That is what we did: we added evil to evil, sin to sin.

“That this is a rebellious people.” God is speaking of the Israelites: we are a rebellious people. We don’t want to hear nothing: brother, you can’t teach me nothing. Then you are going to die in your sin.

“Lying children.” We love lies. Why do you think our people go to church every Sunday? Our people will kill you for the truth and give you the biggest hug for lies. When you were in the world selling drugs, your family loved you; now you are in the truth, they hate your guts. Our people love evil. All this killing you see happening: do not think those people were righteous, and don’t think you are better than them either. The Most High God must kill two-thirds so that one-third can get it. Some of our people you cannot rule a kingdom with; they are evil beyond evil, and God will kill them so that you can rule.

“Children that will not hear the law of the Lord.” Our people hate God’s laws. Sis, the Bible says you cannot wear pants; I don’t want to hear that. You mean Daddy is going to kill me because I don’t have a beard, because I don’t have the fringes, because I eat pork? Yes, he is going to put you to death. That is not us saying it; that is what God said.

“Which say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not”: don’t see my sin, don’t see my evil, don’t tell me what is about to happen.

“Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits.” Don’t prophesy the truth to us; tell us lies. Tell me how much Jesus loves me, that God doesn’t kill, that God is love and loves everybody, that we are all one. That is not in the Bible. The white man says we are all one.
“Get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us.” Get away from me with your Bible stuff. Why are you always talking Bible stuff?

“Because ye despise this word”: because you hate my law. “And trust in oppression and perverseness.” Our people trust in oppression. We love the fact that the other nation is on top of us. Esau used the system to cripple us: some of us walk around like we are fine, but we are handicapped mentally.

“And stay thereon.” Some think that when Esau came with let’s integrate, it was because they love you. That is stupid. The white man thinks a hundred years ahead; the negro sitting next to you thinks about tomorrow. After the chains came off, we started successful businesses: our own hospitals, our own schools, our own banks. Then the white man said, let’s integrate them, let’s tell them we are one, because if we leave them segregated we won’t be able to stop them. Even when they bombed us and destroyed Black Wall Street, we still found a way to survive.

Look at Judah, the so-called African-American, here in America. With all the evil the white man did to Judah, Judah still rose up and found a way to educate himself: doctors, lawyers, engineers, teachers, bus drivers, police officers, firefighters. We have been integrated about sixty years. If we had not integrated, think how far we would have gone in those sixty years. Integration made us shut down our hospitals, our schools, our bus system, our clinics, our banks, because the negro said, I want my son in the white school, the white man’s ice is colder than the black man’s ice. Integration handicapped us.

And even after all that, we still succeeded, and they still do not understand how these people keep rising up and standing on their own two feet. That is because we are the Israelites, the greatest people on planet earth, the sons and daughters of the living God.

Integration is leaving one plantation for another; you think integration means you are free, but it is just words on paper. Segregation never went away, not for white people. It is alive right now. And God never taught us to integrate with other nations: he commanded us not to marry them and not to integrate with them. That is a law. God knew that when we integrated with these people, they would make us forget his laws, and that is exactly what happened. We forgot God’s laws, we forgot who we are, and now we think they love us. God commanded us to stay the hell away from white people.

They were all on the same page to steal the land of the Native American Indians with fake papers, and that is still going on today, with black people’s homes being stolen in New York with fake documents. Nothing new under the sun.

“Ye shall inherit their land, and I will give it unto you to possess it, a land that floweth with milk and honey: I am the Lord your God, which have separated you from other people.” God separated us from other people. God doesn’t want us with them.

“Ye shall therefore put difference between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean fowls and clean.” That is clean food and unclean food. God put that there because that nation was eating those things, and he said, you shall not do that.

“And ye shall be holy unto me.” Holy means separate: you shall be separate unto the Lord.

“For I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people.” Sever means separate, and separating is called segregation. “That ye should be mine.”

precepts.why:
“If ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people.” Why does the negro want to be together with them, to be equal? God says we are above. There is no equality and no integration with God. Integration means they are on top and we are on the bottom. God says no: we are on top, the top people on planet earth.

“And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation”: a separate nation. “These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.”

God set our bounds “from the Red sea even unto the sea of the Philistines”, delivered the inhabitants of the land into our hand, and said “thou shalt drive them out before thee.”

“Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.” We should make no covenant with that nation.

“They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee.” This is why segregation should come back. God said they should not live in our land, because they will make us sin against him and worship their god. I don’t want these animals near my house.

Segregation is in the Bible, whatever those say who tell you God changed, there is no more segregation, we are all one, one love. To hell with your one love.

“Take heed to thyself, lest thou make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land whither thou goest, lest it be for a snare in the midst of thee: But ye shall destroy their altars, break their images, and cut down their groves.” Every single Christian church in the black community should shut down. Black people have no business in these churches. They do nothing but push white supremacy on our people, telling you white people are better than you. Let those churches go to the white community where they belong, with white Jesus. But our people will kill you to stay inside them.

“For thou shalt worship no other god: for the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.” Make a covenant with them, “and they go a whoring after their gods”: you start marrying their women and their men, and then you start worshipping their gods just to please them, putting the true God off to the side.

“And thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters go a whoring after their gods, and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods.” There is no interracial marriage in the Bible. There is no such thing as you love who you love; that is not in the scriptures. God said do not give your daughters to their sons and do not take their daughters for your sons. The dumb pastors say forget what God said.

And what they did back then is still going on. Black homeowners in Brooklyn are losing their homes to deed theft, men coming with fake court orders to houses families have lived in for years, the same fake papers they used on the so-called American Indians. That is Amalek. And you still think these people love you?

When God brings us into the land and casts out “the Hittites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than thou”: “thou shalt smite them, and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them.” He keeps saying the same thing: make no covenant with them.

“Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son. For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods.” God said do not marry these people.

“Ye shall destroy their altars, and break down their images, and cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire.” Not that anyone should go burn the Christian churches; they should all just shut down.

“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God”: a separate people. “The Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.” That cannot happen if you are integrated with everybody. When the white man says we are one, he means, as long as I am on top of you. As long as you are on the bottom, working for them, while they own your hospitals and the school system that teaches your children to be stupid, we are one. Don’t let them fool you.

Why did God choose us? “The Lord did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people: But because the Lord loved you.” God chose the Israelites as his special people because he loves us, and because he kept the oath he swore to our fathers.

For the dumb Christian who thinks there is no segregation in the Bible: “For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God”, a separate people, “and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.”

How many times does God have to say the same thing? We are above. But the black man, the Hispanic man and the Native American man cannot see it: no, we are equal. No, we are not equal. There is no equality.

This is after Nehemiah came back to the land. “All they that had separated themselves from the people of the lands unto the law of God, their wives, their sons, and their daughters”: we separated ourselves from their women and from their children.

“They clave to their brethren, their nobles, and entered into a curse, and into an oath, to walk in God’s law, which was given by Moses the servant of God”, “And that we would not give our daughters unto the people of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons.”

Before that we were marrying them. When Nehemiah came back and read us the law, we separated from them and put them out: take your kids, you’ve got to go. You cannot tell a negro that today, and you definitely cannot tell a Christian that today: I’m not going to leave my white woman. But that is what the Bible says.

“But know that the Lord hath set apart him that is godly for himself.” God has separated the righteous for himself. We are the righteous; they are the evil. We are the light; they are the darkness. Some of us don’t want that: I don’t want to be on an island by myself. That is exactly what God wants, us on an island by ourselves.

“The Lord will hear when I call unto him.” The only way the Lord will hear when you call is if you separate yourself. We need to separate from these people.

sense.text:
Section 8 and the welfare system damaged the black family and produced a lot of handicaps in our community. Section 8 was never made for you to be on it year after year; it was made to get you on your feet. Use it, don’t abuse it, and many of us abused it. Now the government says two years and you are out. That law is going to force us to become something and to work together. The system was never created for you to succeed; it was created to destroy you. This thing must happen, and it is going to get worse.

That is what God said: “Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble.” Jacob’s trouble. A sister bragging that the government pays her rent while she buys luxury bags and swipes her EBT card has no idea what is coming. God has to turn up the heat on our people for us to change.

When you look at a tree, don’t look at the leaves; look at the root. No tree starts from the top. When you look at a problem, look at the root of it.

“Marriage is honourable in all.” All through the Bible it speaks of marriage. The system takes that out of a sister’s mind: sis, if you sleep with this man and get pregnant, the government will help you. If the system were not in place, she would get married. Stop thinking the white man is stupid, and stop thinking he created this because he loves you and wants to help you. He created it to destroy you mentally.

Women control sex; men control marriage. Every black woman should be married, and they are not because they do not understand what they have. If she controls sex, no man has her until he marries her, and men start to look at women differently: that is a beautiful sister, she knows her worth, I’m not going to turn her into a hoe. When the next man shows up with the same game, she says, hold up, I’m not going to be a single mother again; I want to get to know you so we can build a family together. That is how she should think. But because of the system, she doesn’t.

precepts.why:
The first man came, she got pregnant; a mistake, fine, she should learn. But the next man showed up and she did the same, and the third, and the fourth: baby after baby. Why? Because in her mind, the more babies, the more food stamps, the more rooms in the Section 8. That is a slavery mindset, a destructive, insane mindset.

“And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you.” God said the men that hate you, the men that despise you, are going to rule over you. So what makes you think the system he built is in your favor? What makes you think the system he built is for you to succeed? You are crazy if you think that.

sense.text:
This is the law God set up. “For the poor shall never cease out of the land.” The poor are always going to be there, as Christ said the poor are always with us; that is where he got it from. There are always going to be poor among our people for us to help.

Even the richest of our people, Jay-Z, LeBron, still go to the white hospital and the white supermarket the same as the homeless black man on the streets of Atlanta. From the top of our people to the poorest, we all depend on white institutions. That is integration. They could not stand black unity and could not control us segregated, so they integrated to know what we are doing and get our money, and everything we owned is gone. Now we have to go to them.

precepts.why: “I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.” Why? Because the Most High always sends somebody to come and help.

This is the law for the poor. “If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren within any of thy gates in thy land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother: But thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need.”

If there is a poor brother or sister in the midst of us, God commands us to help them. That is the law.

sense.text:
Some of us in this country have more than we need. Black people are the biggest consumers in America, the biggest consumer on earth; we have things in our houses we never wear, still in the package. We have been spoiled by the system, and that is why some cannot see themselves outside America. Some have good jobs, the white man has paid you well, and you never think: what if God took everything away tomorrow? Could I survive? It can happen.

“There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching.” Here is a man who worked hard and became rich: he got paid well, a nice house, nice cars, top notch, he and his wife living well.

“Whereas he saith, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods.” He is going to keep on eating, and he doesn’t give a damn about his brothers and his sisters.

“And yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him.” He has no idea what is about to happen tomorrow; he thinks he is always going to be good. What if tomorrow he has a heart attack and drops dead? “And that he must leave those things to others, and die.” You work all your life and build wealth, and then you leave it to somebody who never worked for it. Leave it to your children, and if they turn out knuckleheads addicted to drugs, forty or fifty years of building is gone in less than five.

Some are so ignorant they say, hell with you poor people; I don’t want my children in a black school, I want to live next to white folks and eat at a white restaurant. The system co-opted you. You do not know what is going to happen tomorrow.
A rich man came and asked Christ this question, and Christ answered him: “Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God: but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.”
“All these things have I kept from my youth up: what lack I yet?” He tells Christ, I keep all these laws you just named; what is it I need to get the kingdom?

“If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor.” Christ is not telling him to sell everything and be homeless. He is saying: help your brothers, help your sisters in need. You have enough to help; why don’t you want to help them?
“He went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions.” He had great riches and great possessions, but he was not helping his brothers and his sisters.

“A rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven.” It does not say a rich man cannot get the kingdom. Christ is saying it is going to be hard, because you have been spoiled. Here in Georgia there is money, and some of our people are so well off they will not repent: I don’t need God. They are going to die. They gain the whole world and lose their soul.

“It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.” The scripture says we are commanded to help each other in need.

We need to learn how to work together, because of the time of Jacob’s trouble. Look at the welfare system now and how many of our people have become homeless. We cannot turn our backs on them. We cannot let brothers and sisters sleep in the street with their children, here and outside of America, and for that we have to come together. That is why the donations are so important. At the end of the day, those are our brothers and sisters.

Agabus “signified by the spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world.” A great dearth is a famine.

“Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judea.” According to his ability: we do not all have the same. Some have more than others, but whatever you can give, give. That is why, when Christ told the young man to sell and give to the poor, he was not saying sell your home and become homeless; he was saying give according to your ability. They came together and gave according to their ability to send relief to the brothers and sisters in need.

We are doing the same thing. We send packages to brothers and sisters in different places in Africa almost every month, and keep storage units of things for those in need outside of America. That is what the pantry is for. If you go hungry, shame on you: when you are hungry is not the time for pride, and your pride will kill you. Bishop put in place that every single school, not only in America, should have a pantry to help brothers and sisters with food; even in Liberia at Passover, the pantry was there.

precepts.why:
Some think this is not scripture. It is. “And all that believed were together, and had all things common”: unity. They came together and learned how to work together. That is the spirit being brought back to our people.

“And sold their possessions and goods.” They did not sell their homes and become homeless. They had extra, and they sold their extra to help their brothers and sisters. “And parted them to all men, as every man had need”: one has five children and another has one; one family needs five bags of rice and the other needs one. The bigger the family, the more food they need, so they distributed according to need.

“And they, continuing daily with one accord”: one spirit, one mind. “And breaking bread from house to house, did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart”: they came together and ate together.

“Praising God”, giving glory to the Most High, “and having favour with all the people. And the Lord added to the church daily.” God blessed them.

“There arose a murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration.” The twelve said, “It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables. Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.” They set up a food distribution, to make sure everybody had something to eat, because the widows were being neglected.

Every one of us should have that same spirit. In Liberia an older sister said that if it were not for the brothers of the congregation, she would not eat: they visit her and bring her food every day. So when sisters give birth, a team goes to cook for the family; when people are in the hospital, a team goes to visit. A sister in Orlando was found because the sisters noticed she was missing at the Sabbath and went to visit, and found she had passed away. When people have not been heard from, ask what happened to them.

The Most High put this in the Bible because it is going to happen. Not only should there be a pantry here; every one of us should have a pantry in our house, food stored up just in case. If a civil war broke out and every grocery store shut down, what would you do? A stupid man says that can never happen; you forgot where you are. This is America. Prepare spiritually, and prepare physically.

sense.text:
Stop stressing over Esau’s jobs. Esau doesn’t give a damn about any of you. Some of you stress and get depressed over a company that does not belong to you, and it is going to bring death on you. You are just a number; the minute you drop dead you are replaced before you are in the grave. Go to work, do the best you can, and go home, because when you drop dead the only ones who lose are your wife and your children.

“Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on.” Christ says don’t worry about what you are going to eat, what you are going to drink, or what you are going to wear.

“Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?” When was the last time you saw a bird plant anything? The bird doesn’t plant and doesn’t work, yet God finds a way to feed it every day. You are more important to God than the bird. The bird doesn’t worry about how it is going to eat tomorrow; why do you?
“Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?” By stressing and worrying, can you change anything? Can you change tomorrow? Then why are you worried about tomorrow?

“Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow.” The lily is a flower; it doesn’t go to work, yet it lives. “Shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?”

You are more important to God than the grass outside.

“For after all these things do the Gentiles seek.” The other nations have to worry about these things, not you. Some of us are stressed because we have very small faith, or no faith at all. Build your faith up; ask God to increase your faith. “For your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.”

“But seek ye first the kingdom of God.” Some are so stressed they can’t even open the Bible to read, so stressed they can’t fall asleep. Seek first the kingdom of God “and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.” If you do what the Bible says, you should not worry about anything. As long as you stay in the Bible and keep the laws, don’t worry about everything else.

“Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself.” Let tomorrow worry about itself. The problem is that some of us are never satisfied and never have enough. How many here have no food at home, no water, no clothes on their back, no house to cover them? None.
